items.title: Algorithmic Visualizer 3D
items.description: Interactive platform for real-time visualization of sorting algorithms, graph traversal (Dijkstra, A*), and search trees.
items.longDescription: Developed to consolidate core Computer Science studies. Demonstrates step-by-step execution states, compares time and space Big-O complexities, and allows testing with custom datasets.
items.problem: Studying graph traversal and tree algorithms abstractly often lacks real-time visual inspection of internal memory states, exploration frontiers, and asymptotic cost.
items.objective: Engineer an interactive browser-based graphics engine capable of executing and stepping through classic algorithms without blocking the main UI thread.
items.solution: Decoupled architecture leveraging Web Workers for computing algorithmic state transitions and the HTML5 Canvas API for smooth 60fps rendering.
process: Modeled core data structures (weighted graphs, search trees, and arrays) in strict TypeScript.
Implemented deterministic state snapshot generators to support stepping forward, pausing, and speed control.
Offloaded heavy algorithmic computation into Web Workers to keep the UI responsive under dense inputs.
features: Dynamic inspection of sorting algorithms and binary search trees.
Real-time comparison of time and space Big-O complexity.
Custom dataset and graph topology input controls.

items.title: DevNexus — Collaborative Code Platform
items.description: Full-stack application featuring secure authentication, a real-time collaborative code editor, and snippet sharing among developers.
items.longDescription: Distributed system powered by WebSockets for collaborative editing synchronization, MongoDB persistence, and in-memory caching for frequent query optimization.
items.problem: Remote code reviews and pair-programming sessions require instantaneous state synchronization across multiple connected clients without write conflicts.
items.objective: Build a low-latency collaborative full-stack environment with document persistence and secure session management.
items.solution: Bidirectional WebSocket communication in Node.js paired with MongoDB document storage and an in-memory caching layer for high-frequency reads.
process: Designed a lightweight WebSocket event protocol for streaming edit deltas and active participant states.
Modeled MongoDB schemas for snippet versioning and access permissions.
Crafted a responsive React and Tailwind CSS workspace with live connection telemetry.
features: Real-time collaborative code editing powered by WebSockets.
Secure user authentication and session management.
In-memory caching layer for fast recurring query resolution.

items.title: Distributed API Gateway & Task Manager
items.description: High-performance FastAPI microservice with asynchronous task queues, intelligent rate limiting, and system health monitoring.
items.longDescription: Focused on software engineering and backend architecture: concurrent processing with Celery, JWT authentication, automated Swagger documentation, and Docker containerization.
items.problem: Traditional synchronous APIs suffer severe latency spikes when handling traffic bursts or compute-intensive background operations.
items.objective: Design a resilient backend architecture that decouples request ingestion from heavy execution through distributed queues.
items.solution: Python/FastAPI service using Redis as both a message broker and rate-limiting store, Celery workers for concurrent execution, PostgreSQL for ACID persistence, and Docker for orchestration.
process: Built asynchronous FastAPI endpoints with strict schema validation and automated OpenAPI/Swagger specs.
Implemented Redis-backed rate limiting and dispatched long-running jobs to Celery worker pools.
Containerized the full stack (API, Celery Workers, Redis, and PostgreSQL) using Docker.
features: Concurrent background task execution with Celery and Redis.
Intelligent rate limiting and JWT-based authentication.
System health check endpoints and interactive Swagger documentation.
Fully containerized Docker setup with transactional PostgreSQL storage.

items.title: Sentiment Classifier & NLP Pipeline
items.description: Natural Language Processing pipeline with model fine-tuning for sentiment analysis and automated user feedback classification.
items.longDescription: End-to-end implementation covering text preprocessing, tokenization, embedding extraction, and high-availability inference endpoint deployment.
items.problem: Manually evaluating large volumes of user feedback is slow and inconsistent, requiring models capable of capturing subtle semantic context.
items.objective: Build an end-to-end Natural Language Processing pipeline — from corpus preprocessing and model fine-tuning to production inference serving.
items.solution: Fine-tuned Transformer model using PyTorch and Hugging Face, paired with a standardized tokenization pipeline and served via a containerized FastAPI endpoint.
process: Executed corpus cleaning, text normalization, tokenization, and embedding extraction.
Fine-tuned and evaluated the PyTorch model across validation splits.
Packaged the trained model behind a FastAPI REST inference service inside Docker.
features: Automated text preprocessing and tokenization pipeline.
Semantic embedding extraction and sentiment classification with PyTorch & Hugging Face.
Low-latency REST inference endpoint served via FastAPI.
Interactive web interface for live sentence evaluation.
